changeeol

Normalize a text file to Unix newlines

Stata 

changeeol source.txt destination.txt, eol(unix)

R base 

writeBin(charToRaw(paste0(paste(readLines(src),collapse='\n'),'\n')),dst)

Fixed workflow example; adapt the object and column names together.

Stata reference · R reference

Write text using explicit Windows CRLF bytes

Stata 

changeeol source.txt destination.txt, eol(windows)

R base 

writeBin(charToRaw(paste0(paste(readLines(src),collapse='\r\n'),'\r\n')),dst)

Fixed workflow example; adapt the object and column names together.

Stata reference · R reference

checksum

Compute a file integrity digest

Stata 

checksum sample.txt

R tools 

tools::md5sum(src)

MD5 is a workflow alternative: Stata checksum uses POSIX CRC, so digest values are not comparable.

Stata reference · R reference

Save a file digest in a sidecar text file

Stata 

checksum sample.txt, saving(sample.sum)

R tools 

digest <- tools::md5sum(src); writeLines(unname(digest),dst)

Writes an R MD5 sidecar, not a Stata .sum file; Stata cannot validate this format as its CRC sidecar.

Stata reference · R reference

copy

Copy a local file to a new path

Stata 

copy source.txt destination.txt

R base 

file.copy(src,dst,overwrite=FALSE)

src and dst are temporary paths in this runnable fixture; no network transfer is involved.

Stata reference · R reference

Overwrite a destination file with a local copy

Stata 

copy source.txt destination.txt, replace

R base 

file.copy(src,dst,overwrite=TRUE)

Demonstrates overwrite on newly created temporary files only.

Stata reference · R reference

dir

List CSV files in a directory

Stata 

dir "*.csv"

R base 

list.files(path,pattern='[.]csv$',full.names=FALSE)

Fixed workflow example; adapt the object and column names together.

Stata reference · R reference

List files including hidden dot files

Stata 

dir, all

R base 

list.files(path,all.files=TRUE,no..=TRUE)

Differs from Stata R all.files includes dot files; hidden-file conventions vary by operating system.

file

Read one line through a text connection

Stata 

file open handle using sample.txt, read text
file read handle line
file close handle

R base 

con <- file(src,open='rt',encoding='UTF-8'); line <- readLines(con,n=1); close(con)

Fixed workflow example; adapt the object and column names together.

Stata reference · R reference

Write and close a UTF-8 text connection

Stata 

file open handle using sample.txt, write text
file write handle "hello" _n
file close handle

R base 

con <- file(path,open='wt',encoding='UTF-8'); writeLines('hello',con); close(con)

The example closes its own temporary connection explicitly.

Stata reference · R reference

filefilter

Replace literal text throughout a small file

Stata 

filefilter source.txt destination.txt, from("old") to("new")

R base 

writeLines(gsub('old','new',readLines(src),fixed=TRUE),dst,useBytes=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Line-oriented small-file workflow; binary patterns and large-file streaming are not covered.

Stata reference · R reference

Replace tab separators in a text file

Stata 

filefilter source.txt destination.txt, from(\t) to(";")

R base 

writeLines(gsub('\t',';',readLines(src),fixed=TRUE),dst,useBytes=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Literal small-text-file replacement; quoted delimiters in tabular data need a parser instead.

Stata reference · R reference

Find a named file inside a specified directory

Stata 

findfile sample.txt, path(folder)

R base 

found <- list.files(folder,pattern='^sample[.]txt$',full.names=TRUE); stopifnot(length(found)==1L); normalizePath(found,winslash='/')

Fixed workflow example; adapt the object and column names together.

10 more examples and alternatives

Import a CSV file with a header

Stata 

import delimited using sample.csv, clear

R utils 

data <- utils::read.csv(path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

Fixed workflow example; adapt the object and column names together.

Stata reference · R reference

Read a selected range of text rows

Stata 

import delimited using sample.csv, rowrange(3:4) varnames(nonames) clear

R utils 

data <- utils::read.csv(path,header=FALSE,skip=2,nrows=2,col.names=c('id','x'))

Differs from Stata Row numbers refer to physical file rows including the header; R column names are fixed in this example.

Stata reference · R reference

Preserve zero-padded identifiers during import

Stata 

import delimited using sample.csv, stringcols(1) clear

R utils 

data <- utils::read.csv(path,colClasses=c('character','numeric'))

Fixed workflow example; adapt the object and column names together.

Stata reference · R reference

Import a CSV file without a header

Stata 

import delimited using sample.csv, varnames(nonames) clear

R utils 

data <- utils::read.csv(path,header=FALSE,col.names=c('id','x'))

Differs from Stata R column names id and x are supplied explicitly; Stata would choose default names without further renaming.

jdbc

Append controlled rows to an existing SQL table

Stata 

jdbc insert id score, table("people")

R DBI 

DBI::dbAppendTable(con,'people',data); observed <- DBI::dbReadTable(con,'people'); DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

Requires an existing Stata DSN/JDBC connection for the shown Stata example. The controlled SQLite fixture verifies the SQL/table operation, not ODBC/JDBC driver connection; use an appropriate DBI backend in production.

Stata reference · R reference

Load an entire SQL table through a DBI backend

Stata 

jdbc load, table("people")

R DBI 

data <- DBI::dbReadTable(con,'people'); DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

Requires an existing Stata DSN/JDBC connection for the shown Stata example. The controlled SQLite fixture verifies the SQL/table operation, not ODBC/JDBC driver connection; use an appropriate DBI backend in production.

Stata reference · R reference

mkdir

Create a directory

Stata 

mkdir work

R base 

dir.create(path)

The runnable fixture creates a new directory under R's temporary directory.

Stata reference · R reference

odbc

Inspect database table field names

Stata 

odbc describe "people", dsn("research")

R DBI 

fields <- DBI::dbListFields(con,'people'); DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

Requires an existing Stata DSN/JDBC connection for the shown Stata example. The controlled SQLite fixture verifies the SQL/table operation, not ODBC/JDBC driver connection; use an appropriate DBI backend in production. This row returns names only, not the Stata column-type report.

Stata reference · R reference

Load selected rows from a SQL query

Stata 

odbc load, exec("SELECT id, score FROM people WHERE score >= 20") dsn("research")

R DBI 

data <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con,'SELECT id, score FROM people WHERE score >= 20 ORDER BY id'); DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

Requires an existing Stata DSN/JDBC connection for the shown Stata example. The controlled SQLite fixture verifies the SQL/table operation, not ODBC/JDBC driver connection; use an appropriate DBI backend in production.

Stata reference · R reference

Inspect available tables in a database

Stata 

odbc query "research"

R DBI 

tables <- DBI::dbListTables(con); DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

Requires an existing Stata DSN/JDBC connection for the shown Stata example. The controlled SQLite fixture verifies the SQL/table operation, not ODBC/JDBC driver connection; use an appropriate DBI backend in production.

save

Save a table as a current Stata DTA file

Stata 

save sample.dta, replace

R haven 

haven::write_dta(data,path)

Differs from Stata R object names are not stored as Stata's active-data state; haven writes supported Stata metadata.

Stata reference · R reference

saveold

Write a Stata 12-compatible DTA file

Stata 

saveold sample.dta, version(12) replace

R haven 

haven::write_dta(data,path,version=12)

Differs from Stata Use names accepted by haven's older-format validation; this fixture uses names of at least two characters.

Stata reference · R reference

savespss

Save the data as an SPSS file

Stata 

savespss "data.sav", replace

R haven 

haven::write_sav(data, path)

Differs from Stata Community command. haven writes variable and value labels, but rejects Stata tagged missing values (.a, .b) with an error. Convert them explicitly to ordinary NA or to chosen SPSS user-missing codes with haven::labelled_spss() before writing. String widths and display formats may differ.

Stata reference · R reference

setroot

Locate a project root from a marker file

Stata 

setroot

R rprojroot 

root <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file('.here'),path=child)

Uses the explicit .here marker and a supplied starting path; the Stata command also supports other markers and stores a global macro.
